messages:
Alex (Sales): Need help reconciling an airfare charge. Corpcard shows $842.70 charged to \"UNITED AIRLINES\" on 2026-09-10. Ticket was refundable but I canceled and the airline issued an e-credit minus a $150 change/cancel fee. The corpcard still shows the original charge and the airline emailed an e-credit voucher number only. How do I record this?
Priya (Finance): Do you have the airline confirmation and the e-credit voucher? Also was any part of the ticket client-billable or a personal upgrade?
Alex (Sales): Uploaded vendor emails: https://files.redwood/travel/united_charge_2212.pdf and voucher: https://files.redwood/travel/united_credit_voucher_2212.pdf. The original booking included a $120 seat upgrade that I paid on the corpcard but manager approved. Client paid for main fare 70% and company covers remainder.
Jonah (Travel): Airline policy: e-credits typically post to the original form of payment but sometimes show as a voucher code. If it's a voucher code we can't capture it on the corpcard automatically. Travel team can escalate to the airline to request a refund back to the card for corporate reconciliation. Did you request refund vs voucher?
Alex (Sales): I requested refund but airline only offered e-credit voucher XCV-998877 and said refund would take 7-10 business days and might not be granted for the fare class. They applied the cancel fee $150 and the voucher value equals charge minus fee.
ExpenseBot: :warning: Expense flagged  partial refund/e-credit detected. Policy=refund_vs_voucher. REF: FLT-2212
Priya (Finance): Filing guidance: 1) Submit in Expensify under Travel > Airfare with attachments (ticket pdf, voucher, manager approval). 2) In notes include breakdown: original fare $842.70, cancel fee $150, voucher value $692.70, client-billable portion 70% of fare, seat-upgrade $120 (company paid). 3) For GL: code main fare to GL 6100-Travel-Lodging (split client 70% code CL-710 / company 30% GL 6100), upgrade to GL 6150-Travel-Extras, and record cancel fee to GL 6570-BankFees. If airline does not refund to card, finance will record vendor credit (voucher) as a receivable/contra-charge and track until applied.
Maya (People Ops): Manager approval is in Slack DM (Marta approved earlier). Alex, please attach that screenshot. If any portion is personal (e.g., extra legroom for comfort), mark it as personal and reimburse via payroll.
Alex (Sales): Attached manager_approval_marta.png and ticket_pdf. Submitted Expensify: https://expensify.com/receipt/RE-246700 status pending. Notes: \"Voucher XCV-998877, cancel fee $150, client 70% share, seat upgrade $120 company-paid.\"
Jonah (Travel): I'll open a travel escalation with UNITED referencing voucher XCV-998877 to request card refund. If airline confirms refund to card we'll reconcile and process refund to the corpcard account. If airline keeps voucher, finance will post vendor credit and mark the voucher in our travel ledger for future bookings.
Priya (Finance): One extra: please indicate whether the voucher is transferable to company travel (some vouchers are non-transferable). If transferable we can use it and there's no cashflow issue. If non-transferable we'll treat as vendor receivable and escalate for refund if client reimbursement expected.
Alex (Sales): Airline replied: voucher is transferable to same passenger only, not to company. They declined refund. I've asked for escalation but sounds unlikely.
ExpenseBot: :information_source: FLT-2212 updated: finance created vendor-credit record VC-2212; status = pending-travel-use.
Priya (Finance): Final steps for you: 1) mark Expensify expense as \"pending finance review\"; 2) include a short memo that ticket main fare is client-billable 70% and provide client code CL-710; 3) if voucher remains non-transferable, finance will deduct client reimbursement to reflect effective company cost (we'll discuss adjustments).
Alex (Sales): Done. Marked pending finance review and added client code CL-710. Thanks everyone.
Maya (People Ops): Noted for policy: prefer booking through travel portal to avoid voucher-only outcomes where possible.
Priya (Finance): We'll close FLT-2212 once vendor credit is resolved or applied. For now marking as approved for reimbursement of net company-paid portion (company share minus voucher impact) pending final vendor resolution.
notes: Attach voucher + manager approval; code client share CL-710; finance will treat non-transferable voucher as vendor credit and adjust reimbursement accordingly.
